chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Ṣalt, from Zurʿah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:

Then you recite the talbiyah from al-Masjid al-Ḥarām just as you recited the talbiyah when you entered iḥrām, and you say: “Labbayka for a hajj whose completion and conveyance are upon You.” If you are able, let your departure to Minā be at the decline of the sun; otherwise, then whenever it is made easy for you on the Day of Tarwiyah. This does not conflict with the first two reports, because the one walking recites the talbiyah from the place where he performs salat for iḥrām, while the rider recites the talbiyah at al-Raqṭāʾ or at Shiʿb al-Dubb, and neither of them raises the voice in the talbiyah except when overlooking al-Abṭaḥ. This is indicated by that.

key_terms.الرَّاكِبَ: the rider, whose point of talbiyah is specified separately
key_terms.الْمَاشِيَ: the one traveling on foot, whose point of talbiyah differs in this ruling
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ: the Sacred Mosque in Makkah, from which the talbiyah is initiated here
key_terms.بِحَجَّةٍ: for a hajj; indicating the intention and form of the rite
key_terms.تُلَبِّي: to recite the talbiyah in response to the call of hajj
key_terms.زَوَالَ الشَّمْسِ: the sun’s decline from the meridian, indicating the preferred time of departure
key_terms.مِنًى: Minā, the ritual destination to which one departs on the Day of Tarwiyah
key_terms.يَوْمِ التَّرْوِيَةِ: the eighth of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, the day associated with departure to Minā

ai.seo_question: When should a muḥrim for hajj begin reciting the talbiyah according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling on when the muḥrim for hajj should begin the talbiyah and from where it should be pronounced. It distinguishes between the pedestrian and the rider, and clarifies that the reports on the matter are reconciled by their differing circumstances.
